justification: Critical: changes the granny-flat verdict served by the granny-flat app. Until now every result read 'not yet determined' because the engine had no frontage, battle-axe or s 50 facts; with them, most regular lots in the 28 councils with an LEP land use table get a decided answer per approval path.

pre_impl.existing_data: lep_land_use_table: 19,551 rows over 28 councils, dwelling_houses rows with permissibility permitted / prohibited / exempt. spatial_overlays zone layer gives the council for a point statewide; the height layer used by lookup_lga does not (Greystanes, Cumberland, returned no council, measured 2026-10-09).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: lookup_lga reads the height layer and returned None for Cumberland, so the s 50 check reads the council from the zone layer instead. The SEPP measures frontage at the building line, which equals the front boundary only on a regular lot, so frontage is sent only for a rectangular lot with a confidently identified front.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new tables or columns. Reuses lib/geometry calculateLotDimensions (the verify app's property panel), lep_land_use_table and intelligence_brief._norm_lga. The engine (services/secondary_dwelling_paths.py) is unchanged.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Any missing fact leaves that path 'not determined'. Council outside the 28, no dwelling_houses row, an 'exempt' row or contradictory rows all read s 50 as not established, never permitted.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Two optional request fields (frontage_m, battle_axe) on detect and confirm; approval_paths gains da_attached. No existing field changed type.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Without this every owner was told 'not yet determined' even for a plain 600 m2 R2 lot with a 15 m frontage. The risk the other way is a wrong pass from a mis-measured frontage, which is why frontage is sent only for confident rectangular lots.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_granny_flat_mutation.py tests/test_secondary_dwelling_paths.py -q -o addopts= ; cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest granny canibuildit GrannyFlat
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A pass is reported without its fact: frontage passed on a battle-axe lot, s 50 read as permitted from a missing or contradictory row, or an attached DA treated as open when a dwelling house is prohibited. Each has a test.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed 2026-10-09 against live data: the test lot (R2, 600 m2, 15 m, not battle-axe) returns CDC PASS -> met; Greystanes and Marrickville resolve s 50 = permitted only after the council was read from the zone layer (lookup_lga gave None for Greystanes). 8 new tests; 421 granny-flat and engine tests and 178 Jest tests pass.

functions.name: _dwelling_house_permissible
functions.input: a database connection, the Planning Portal zone code and the lot's latitude and longitude
functions.output: True when the council's LEP land use table permits dwelling houses in the zone, False when it prohibits them
functions.if_none: No council, no zone, no row, an exempt row, contradictory rows or a query error all return None (not established).

functions.name: _approval_paths
functions.input: validated path rules, zone, lot area and the frontage, battle-axe and s 50 facts when known
functions.output: the detached-case CDC and DA answers plus da_attached, the DA answer for an attached granny flat
functions.if_none: Each missing fact makes its path UNKNOWN with the fact named; nothing defaults to a pass.

functions.name: _approval_status
functions.input: the approval_paths result for one lot including the attached DA answer
functions.output: met when CDC passes, a detached DA meets the site area, or an attached DA faces no SEPP lot-area standard
functions.if_none: Anything undecided reads not_determined; outside_scope only when neither path applies in the zone.

values.value: No regulatory number in code; frontage bands and the site area come from the per-path rules, permissibility from lep_land_use_table
values.if_missing: Missing rules 503 as before; a missing land use row leaves s 50 not established.

break_it.scenario: A battle-axe lot with a long boundary that looks like a wide frontage
break_it.what_happens: battle_axe is sent as true and CDC stays UNKNOWN, naming the access-laneway test
break_it.how: battle-axe detection takes precedence over frontage in the proxy; the engine never passes a battle-axe lot on frontage

break_it.scenario: The council is not one of the 28 in lep_land_use_table
break_it.what_happens: s 50 is not established, so both DA answers stay UNKNOWN; CDC can still pass on frontage
break_it.how: no row returns None, never permitted

break_it.scenario: The council has both permitted and prohibited rows for dwelling houses in the zone
break_it.what_happens: s 50 reads not established instead of picking one
break_it.how: only a single unambiguous permissibility is accepted

break_it.scenario: The lot shape is irregular, so the front boundary is not the frontage at the building line
break_it.what_happens: no frontage is sent and CDC stays UNKNOWN
break_it.how: frontage is sent only for a rectangular lot with confidence >= 0.8

break_it.scenario: A dwelling house is prohibited in the zone
break_it.what_happens: both DA answers read NOT_APPLICABLE and the attached DA is not treated as open
break_it.how: _attached_da_open requires the s 53(2)(a) detached-only reason, reached only after s 50 passes

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: after deploy, run the granny-flat check on a regular R2 lot over 450 m2 and confirm a decided CDC answer instead of 'not yet determined'.

real_layer_exempt.services/granny_flat.py: Real database layer exercised 2026-10-09: _dwelling_house_permissible against production for Greystanes and Marrickville returned permitted, and _approval_paths on the test lot returned CDC PASS.
